newsitem.title: USA: Calif. budget committee holds first meeting.
newsitem.headline: Calif. budget committee holds first meeting.

text.p: A panel of six California legislators began the process Tuesday of negotiating a final budget pact for the 1997-1998 fiscal year, but few observers expected a breakthrough by June 15, the state's Constitutional budget deadline.
The budget committee is made up of three senators and three assembly members. They held their first meeting on Tuesday and will probably meet on a daily basis until they reach an agreement.
The committee's goal is to meld the budget packages of the state Assembly and Senate into a single spending plan.

Another team of budget negotiators -- Republican Gov. Pete Wilson and leaders of the state Senate and Assembly known as the "Big Five" -- will try to settle some of this year's most hotly-disputed legislative issues, including welfare reform, tax cuts and school funding.
The Big Five will meet on Wednesday.
The state Constitution calls for the legislature to approve the final budget by June 15. But in recent years the deadline has often been missed.
Observers in Sacramento said they expected the deadline to be missed again this year.
